claims.text: The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a terminal tensile strain of 13.5% at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
Incorporating approximately 5 at.% Nb into HfZrTiTa0.53 will produce a more homogeneous and refined microstructure.
The Nb addition will refine the grain-boundary structure.
The Nb addition will reduce the formation of brittle intergranular phases.
The Nb addition will enhance solid-solution hardening.
The refined microstructure will improve grain-boundary cohesion and integrity.
Improved grain-boundary integrity will reduce or delay intergranular cracking during tensile deformation.
Delayed intergranular cracking will increase tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
The Nb-modified alloy will attain a uniform tensile elongation of approximately 20% or greater.
Increasing elongation from 13.5% to approximately 20% constitutes an improvement of at least 50%.
The Nb-modified alloy will maintain its yield strength within 5–10% of the 786 MPa baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will maintain its compressive strength within 5–10% of the 1314 MPa baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain impact-triggered chemical energy release within approximately 5–10% of the baseline.
The predicted tensile and compressive behavior applies at room temperature and strain rates below 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis does not establish behavior at elevated temperatures or high strain rates.

contradictions.description: An increase from 13.5% to 20% is approximately 48.1%, not at least 50%; a 50% increase would require at least 20.25%.

The 13.5% baseline is described as terminal tensile strain but is used as the baseline for uniform elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct tensile metrics and cannot be treated as interchangeable without additional data.

The design can be read as applying a quasi-static strain-rate limit below 10^-3 s^-1 to all tests, whereas the impact measurement is specified as a high-energy thin-steel-target penetration test, which necessarily operates in a dynamic loading regime.
